dialect.detail: Classic IBM mainframe batch COBOL; uses RECORDING MODE IS F, LABEL RECORDS ARE OMITTED/STANDARD, ASSIGN U-T-SYSOUT/INPUT (JES SYSOUT-style DDnames), GOBACK, and carriage-control output record pattern typical of IBM OS/VS COBOL or VS COBOL II

purpose.domain_detail: Financial reporting — program title 'FINANCIAL REPORT', calls FINARS01 and FINARS02 (likely financial archive/summary routines)
purpose.summary: Batch report program that reads an 80-byte input file containing financial fields, formats each record into a 132-character print line with numeric editing and a computed total, writes paginated output to SYSOUT with headers, and calls two external financial subroutines (FINARS01, FINARS02) before closing files.

notable_features: Carriage-control byte in output record (ASA printer control)
COPY HEADER1 and COPY PAGING copybooks
CALL 'FINARS01' and CALL 'FINARS02' external subprogram calls
88-level condition names for EOF and NEW-PAGE
ZZ,ZZZ,ZZ9 and ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZ9 numeric edit patterns
verdict.notes: File is 102 lines, all padded to column 80 (avg_line_length=80.0, all lines over 72), consistent with fixed-format mainframe source. PROGRAM-ID is MASD but filename is DAMARP01.cbl — possible mismatch or the file is a renamed copy. One line in PROCEDURE DIVISION has a trailing **' which may be a comment artifact or source corruption. COPY members HEADER1 and PAGING are not shown; their contents affect full analysis.
